Location: Northeast & east-central Florida coastal waters – Fernandina Beach to Jupiter Inlet (Atlantic, out to 60 nm)
Item: Gale watch for Florida's Atlantic coast this weekend; offshore gale warning already up
Details: NWS Jacksonville and Melbourne have Gale Watches up for the Atlantic coastal waters. Fernandina Beach to Flagler Beach out 20 nm: NE winds 25–35 kt, gusts to 40 kt, seas 10–15 ft possible, Saturday afternoon through Monday evening (Small Craft Advisory until noon Sat). Flagler Beach to Sebastian Inlet 0–20 nm: NE 20–30 kt, gusts to 35 kt, seas 8–13 ft possible, Saturday evening through Sunday evening. Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet: NE 25–30 kt, gusts to 35 kt, seas 12–15 ft possible, Sunday morning through Sunday evening. Farther out (beyond 60 nm) a Gale Warning is already in effect. Coastal flood watches/advisories also cover much of the coast. Why it matters: this is a multi-day nor'easter-type blow – the outside run between inlets is off the table, and St. Marys, St. Augustine, Ponce and Sebastian inlets will be dangerous with NE swell against the ebb.
When: Gale watch Sat afternoon Oct 24 – Mon evening Oct 26 2026 (varies by zone; see Details)
Notes: What to do: stay inside on the Atlantic ICW this weekend and don't plan an outside hop between inlets until seas drop. Expect higher-than-normal tides and possible flooding at low docks and fixed bridges – coastal flood watches mean less bridge clearance than charted for tall masts near high tide; check tide stations before passing under fixed spans. Double up lines and add chafe gear if you're at a marina facing NE. A watch can be upgraded to a warning – recheck weather.gov Saturday morning. Southeast Georgia waters (Savannah to Fernandina) have the same gale watch. Gulf side: Small Craft Advisory (NE 20–30 kt, seas 6–10 ft) for Tampa Bay, Charlotte Harbor and Gulf waters Bonita Beach to Suwannee River from 5pm Fri through Wed. Map point is St. Augustine Inlet as a representative location.

Location: Harvey Lock, Harvey (GIWW, Harvey Canal at the Mississippi River)
Item: UPDATE: Harvey Lock closed again Oct 22 – reverse head, no reopening time
Details: American Commercial Barge Line's Oct 23 river report says Harvey Lock is closed as of Oct 22 because of reverse head conditions (low Mississippi River stage), and the Corps has no estimated reopening time. This follows the Oct 5 reopening and an Oct 10 pause already in the sheet. Why it matters: Harvey is one of the two GIWW connections between the Mississippi and the waterway west of New Orleans; with it shut, all east-west traffic squeezes through Algiers Lock, and forecasters say the lower Mississippi is heading toward low-water levels again into early November – so this may not be short.
When: Closed since Oct 22 2026; no reopening estimate
Notes: What to do: plan on Algiers Lock as your route between the river and the GIWW west, and expect waits behind commercial tows. Call ahead or hail the lock on VHF before committing; check the Corps New Orleans District lock status page (mvn.usace.army.mil/lockstatus). Uncertainty: this comes from a barge-line report; I couldn't find an official Corps bulletin dated Oct 22. Published Harvey lockmaster numbers vary between sources (504-366-4683 / 504-862-1061), so confirm on VHF. Separately, Leland Bowman Lock (closed Oct 20 by a log in the gate) no longer appears on ACBL's Oct 23 report, which may mean it's back open – not confirmed.

Location: Bay-Waveland Yacht Club, 1 Yacht Club Dr, Bay St. Louis (Mississippi Sound)
Item: Gulf Coast Melges 15 Championship at Bay-Waveland
Details: Bay-Waveland Yacht Club hosts the Gulf Coast Melges 15 Championship this weekend, a two-day one-design dinghy regatta on the Mississippi Sound; sailing instructions were posted Oct 17. Why it matters: a good chance to watch small, quick one-designs race close to shore off Bay St. Louis – and Bay-Waveland is one of the historic clubs of Gulf Coast sailing.
Notes: What to do: if you're anchored or slipped in Bay St. Louis, watch from the harbor breakwater or the beach; give the racecourse a wide berth if you're under way. Club contact: 228-467-4592. Heads-up: NWS has a Small Craft Advisory for parts of the northern Gulf starting Saturday, so racing could be windy or shortened. This is a regional regatta, not part of the class's official 2026 championship series; entry count not published.

Location: Tarpon Springs – along Spring Bayou, 735 Dodecanese Blvd (Sponge Docks)
Details: Two-day free seafood festival hosted by the Tarpon Springs Merchants Association along Spring Bayou near the historic Sponge Docks. Sat 10am–9pm, Sun 10am–5:30pm; pet- and family-friendly. Why it matters: Tarpon Springs on the Anclote River is an easy hop off the Gulf ICW north of Clearwater – a fun stop with Greek food and the sponge fleet.
Notes: What to do: arriving by boat, call ahead to Anclote River marinas or the City of Tarpon Springs docks for a slip – the weekend will be busy. Free parking with shuttles from Splash Park and Tarpon Towers if you come by car. Same weekend as the Florida Seafood Festival in Apalachicola (Nov 6–7) and Taste of Palacios in Texas (Nov 7). The listing URL calls it the '35th annual'; edition number not confirmed for 2026.
